headline: Highest risk is medium: shared project-directory writes can leak prompts and cause output-to-input cascades; no critical compliance or injection pathway is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A and B have a plausible bridge through files: A writes to the project directory by default and has no self-isolation, while B processes documents/images and can run browsers. If A’s generated content is placed into files B ingests, malicious instructions could be treated as data. This is not proven by docs, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF A writes attacker-controlled text into files that B later parses as document content
IF B ingests project-directory files without provenance filtering
mitigations: Separate A and B into different directories
Disable automatic ingestion of newly written files
Add a manual review step before B processes A outputs
Use provenance tags on files passed between agents
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and trust-boundary enforcement

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches generated source code in a shared project directory and has broad network egress; B handles documents and images and can call APIs. If sensitive material enters the shared workspace, either agent may expose it through model/API calls. The profiles do not show PHI or secrets by default, so medium is the highest supported severity.
conditions: IF sensitive documents or source files are placed in the shared project directory
IF either agent forwards file contents to its configured backend or API
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared workspace
Use separate service accounts and API keys
Restrict outbound network access during processing
Review logs for file-content uploads
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, and its instances share state via the project directory. B can run browsers and call APIs, so both can mutate or consume the same workspace artifacts even though B’s write capability is not explicit. Because overlapping mutable access is plausible but not fully documented, uncertainty escalates to medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory at the same time
IF B writes artifacts through browser/API side effects into files A also edits
mitigations: Run agents sequentially, not concurrently
Assign separate working directories
Lock shared files before edits
Avoid browser-driven writes into the project tree
requires-engineering: add workspace locking and conflict detection

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a code generator that writes files then offers to run, while B is a document-processing agent that can turn inputs into structured outputs. If B consumes A’s generated code or text as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into downstream actions or incorrect documents. The profiles do not show explicit verification gates, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF B treats A-generated files as trusted source material
IF A-generated code or text is used to drive B’s outputs without independent checks
mitigations: Require B to cite original sources, not A outputs
Insert a human verification step between agents
Run a diff/checklist on A outputs before B consumes them
Limit A to draft-only generation
requires-engineering: add automated validation between stages

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and the available data shows no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch. A handles generated source code and B handles documents/images, but there is no evidence of regulated data classes like PHI or EU PII. Because the compliance pathway is not documented, only a low residual risk remains.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into either agent
IF deployment policies require residency or retention guarantees not present in the profiles
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in this pair
Document retention and deletion settings
Use region-appropriate hosting
Review vendor compliance claims before deployment
requires-engineering: obtain formal compliance attestations
